source.title: Towards Robust Spiking Neural Networks:Mitigating Heterogeneous Training Vulnerability via Dominant Eigencomponent Projection
source.authors: De-Song Zhang; Jia Hu; G. Min

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some equations and table layout are flattened, but the results needed here are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures Hessian spectral radius and reports how DEP changes it, and argues that reduced sharpness contributes to generalization. Its experiments focus on spiking-network robustness and heterogeneous-poisoning collapse, rather than the claim versions’ natural-label generalization setup.
record.gate_note: The paper's CIFAR/ImageNet test accuracies are robustness results under clean or adversarial inference and poisoning conditions, not measurements of the training–test generalization gap named in these versions. The Hessian spectral-radius comparison is a measured property relevant to V7, but it does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or rank generalization gaps among similarly trained networks.
record.test_reason: No claim version is tested. Section 4.3 measures unscaled Hessian eigenvalues during inference, not V7's magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance or its association with training–test gaps at similarly low training loss. The robustness and poisoning experiments do not test V1–V6 or V8. The generalization argument in Section 3.2 does not establish the specific relationship named in V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors attribute heterogeneous-training collapse in direct-encoded, BPTT-trained SNNs to amplified Hessian eigenvalues and conclude that DEP reduces measured spectral radius and improves robustness, with a clean-accuracy cost. They report avoiding full collapse with DEP, despite substantial remaining degradation under poisoning.
record.recipe_differences: DEP projects a dominant gradient component during SNN training; the study evaluates robustness, Hessian values, and poisoning-induced collapse rather than the claim versions’ generalization-gap experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Poisoning strength, poisoning scheme, dataset, and inference attack condition change the reported robustness outcomes; the paper reports lower Hessian spectral radius for DEP across the measured clean, FGSM, and PGD inference conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 reports lower inference-time Hessian spectral radius with DEP across four datasets and clean, FGSM, and PGD conditions; for clean CIFAR-10 it falls from 261.94 to 209.90. This is not magnitude-aware sharpness or a generalization-gap comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DEP reduces the measured inference-time Hessian spectral radius of the evaluated spiking networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 shows a clean-accuracy cost alongside improved adversarial accuracy. On vanilla-trained CIFAR-10, clean accuracy falls from 93.75% to 90.21%, while PGD accuracy rises from 0.03% to 31.44%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DEP trades some clean accuracy for improved adversarial robustness in the evaluated spiking networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.4 reports mitigation of heterogeneous-training collapse, with substantial residual degradation. Under c/+p_0 on CIFAR-10, clean accuracy falls from 90.21% without poisoning to 12.07% with five poisoned batches per epoch.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DEP mitigates heterogeneous-training collapse but does not prevent severe poisoning-induced accuracy losses.

record.problems: The paper reports standard deviations for Hessian metrics, but the flattened table layout obscures some dataset-to-value alignment. Robustness accuracy results do not test the natural-label training–test generalization gap in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were retained: the reported test accuracies concern adversarial robustness and heterogeneous-poisoning degradation, not the versioned generalization-gap outcomes. Hessian spectral-radius measurements are relevant to the broad claim topic but do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness criterion or its ranking of generalization gaps.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning; all reported experiments use SGD.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across training regimes.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the reader's V7 tested_not_extracted assessment to untested and its tests/T5 classification to discusses/T6. The omitted results are already declared in rows_left_out and do not warrant missing entries for these versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test generalization.
Width scaling beyond interpolation and test error.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.

The study measures Hessian spectral radius for DEP-trained and vanilla SNNs, but does not measure magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or compare generalization gaps among networks with similarly low training loss.
Removing memorized examples and its effect on test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
